title: A Sharp Classical-to-Quantum Memory Boundary in a One-Slot Partial-SWAP Open-System Process
content: Distinguishing environmental quantum memory from classical temporal correlations requires an operationally specified comparison class. We analyze a fixed-preparation, single-intervention-slot qubit process comprising a partial-SWAP system–environment collision, arbitrary completely positive intermediate system interventions, environmental depolarizing storage noise, and an inverse collision. In the conditional-instrument definition of classical memory, we prove a sharp transition: for every interior angle 0 < θ < π/2, the process has a classical-memory realization if and only if the environmental depolarizing shrinkage satisfies η ≤ 1/3. The forward construction uses an explicit tetrahedral measure-and-prepare channel; the converse follows from a negative three-dimensional principal minor of the partial transpose of the process Choi operator. At the endpoint angles the process instead admits a classical-memory realization for every η. We give a tomographically complete set of sixteen intermediate interventions and independently verify the analytic minor and the corresponding partial-transpose spectrum. A comparison with an existing local concurrence-based witness distinguishes mathematical detection thresholds from measurement-resource performance. Our result is a model-specific exact boundary, not a general equivalence between positive partial transpose and classical memory, and the endpoint classification relies on a fixed, known initial system preparation. This establishes a model-specific process benchmark rather than a general PPT characterisation or a demonstrated quantum-algorithm speedup.
